subject: Greenline model-fit & eval — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Greenline model-fit & eval — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Laura — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a concrete plan to get a Greenline-specific benchmark running on Redwood.

Call highlights (very short):
- Goal: assess model fit for triage assistant + clinical summary drafts (safety + factuality are primary).
- Data: you can provide a de-identified CSV or JSONL with ~1k representative cases for an initial run.
- Timeline: preliminary bench in 7–10 business days after we have the sample and access.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share an anonymized sample (5–50 rows ok for first test). I attached a small example_test_batch.jsonl showing the required fields and prompt template.
2) We confirm security: Private S3 or Google Drive with read-only link + least-privileged temporary token works.
3) Redwood runs baseline with 3 candidate model profiles, returns per-case scores and a summary report.
4) We review together in a short sync (30 min) to pick a follow-up larger run if the results look promising.

What we'll run (baseline):
- small: Llama-2-13B (int8 quant) — low latency baseline
- medium: RedInstruct-7B (recommended for instruction tuning on clinical prompts) — cost-efficient
- large: Falcon-40B-v2 (fp16) — quality-oriented baseline

Scoring we propose: exact-match for structured fields, BLEU-like overlap + clinical factuality checks (annotator-assisted) and hallucination flag rate. We'll provide scoring thresholds and a per-case flagging UI.

Attachments: example_test_batch.jsonl (template), prompt_templates.md (inline short examples).

Ask: Laura — can you drop a short sample (anonymized) to the Drive link in this thread or reply with an attachment? Also confirm any additional HIPAA/BAA constraints so we can route to Private deployment if needed.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Greenline model-fit & eval — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Laura — thanks for the sample and the S3 preference. Quick technical answers and a proposed minimal scoring spec so you know what we'll deliver in the first run.

1) Schema and formats
- CSV is fine for a first pass; we'll convert to JSONL internally. Required fields we need for the baseline run: case_id, encounter_text (string), expected_summary (optional but preferred), expected_triage_label (optional). Metadata columns OK but not required.
- If you prefer JSONL, each line should be a JSON object with keys: case_id, encounter_text, gold_summary, gold_triage_label. We attached bench_spec_v1.pdf with an example and allowed field values.

2) Scoring and outputs
- Automated metrics we run: ROUGE-L and token-overlap for free-text summaries, exact-match and macro-F1 for triage labels, and hallucination-rate estimate (precision of factual assertions using factuality classifier + heuristic entity overlap).
- Per-case outputs: generated_summary (one per model), triage_label, metric scores, and a short auto-generated hallucination_hint (1–2 sentences) that points to mismatches. This hint is generated by the same pipeline but flagged as heuristic — we recommend human review for final decisioning.
- We will also produce a leaderboard CSV and a short 2-page executive summary PDF with recommendations.

3) Candidate models and knobs
- We'll run the three profiles Jordan listed. For each profile we'll: (a) run the prompt templates you approved, (b) evaluate with default decoding (top-k/top-p as per profile), (c) include a quantized variant to compare latency/cost.

4) Security & environment
- Presigned S3 link is perfect. If the BAA is required beforehand, we can run the eval under a limited-data engagement that obfuscates any remaining PHI and ensures logs don't leave your VPC (we can use Redwood Private). We'll need a quick procurement contact to iterate the BAA.

Proposed timeline (if we have sample + S3 link by EOD Nov 10):
- Nov 11–13: Baseline runs (small sample + quick scoring)
- Nov 15: Internal QA and generation of executive summary
- Nov 16–18: Joint review and next-steps planning

Action items for Greenline:
- Share presigned S3 read-only link to the sample by Nov 10 EOD
- Confirm whether the 30-row sample is representative of triage cases (if not, flag which rows are dev/test)
- Provide procurement contact for BAA/DPA conversation (optional for the limited run, required for production)

I've attached bench_spec_v1.pdf with the JSONL example and our exact metric definitions. If you'd like, we can also include a small human-annotation pool to validate hallucination flags for a subset of cases (adds ~2–3 days).

Cheers — Ben
